name: Metro MAN - HQ + 2 remote sites + FinTech colo

rationale.subject: Profile 'metro_man'
rationale.justification: 4 metro sites: each remote site is dual-homed to the HQ hub over two physically diverse paths (primary dark fiber, secondary carrier EVPL) so a single fiber cut never isolates a site.

rationale.subject: Interior gateway protocol
rationale.justification: Design spans 4 geographically separate sites. Each remote site gets its own area (HQ=Area 0, REMOTE-A=Area 1, REMOTE-B=Area 2, COLO=Area 0) attached to backbone Area 0 at HQ. This isolates routing domains: a flapping metro/WAN link only triggers SPF inside its own area, while other areas receive a single Type-3 summary LSA from the ABR. Combined with per-site summary blocks this keeps LSDB size and SPF cost bounded as sites grow.

rationale.subject: Route summarization
rationale.justification: Hierarchical VLSM gave every site one contiguous power-of-two block, so the ABR advertises exactly one summary per area instead of every VLAN. Summaries hide internal flaps from the rest of the network and shrink every routing table.

rationale.subject: Failure detection
rationale.decision: BFD 300 ms x 3 on WAN/MAN links
rationale.justification: Resiliency is 'dual-homed': OSPF's default dead interval (40 s) is far too slow for a FinTech/latency-sensitive network. BFD detects a dead path in <= 900 ms and tells OSPF to reconverge onto the secondary path immediately.

rationale.subject: HQ-REMA-PRIMARY
rationale.justification: Selected OS2 Single-Mode Fiber because link distance (15 km) exceeds the 400 m attenuation/dispersion limit of OM4 Multimode Fiber. Optical budget for 10GBASE-ER @1550 nm: Tx(min) -4.7 dBm - Rx sensitivity -15.8 dBm = 11.1 dB. Plant loss = 15 km x 0.25 dB/km + 2 connectors x 0.5 dB + splices = 4.95 dB, leaving 6.15 dB (>= 3.0 dB required margin). Receiver overload check: Tx(max) 4.0 dBm - 4.95 dB = -0.95 dBm exceeds the -1.0 dBm overload point, so a 2 dB inline attenuator is required.

rationale.subject: HQ-REMA-SECONDARY
rationale.justification: This path is a carrier EVPL (Ethernet Virtual Private Line, MEF E-Line) over 18 km of provider fiber, chosen as the physically diverse secondary path so a single dark-fiber cut cannot isolate the site. The provider owns the optical budget; the enterprise only needs a short single-mode 1000BASE-LX SFP handoff to the carrier NID. EVPL is VLAN-aware, so the service can carry 802.1Q-tagged traffic. Estimated one-way latency 0.5882 ms (0.0882 ms propagation + 0.5 ms carrier switching).

rationale.subject: HQ-REMB-PRIMARY
rationale.justification: 10GBASE-ER reach (40 km) covers 35 km, but loss 10.35 dB + 3.0 dB safety margin = 13.35 dB exceeds its 11.1 dB power budget.

rationale.subject: HQ-REMB-PRIMARY
rationale.justification: Selected OS2 Single-Mode Fiber because link distance (35 km) exceeds the 400 m attenuation/dispersion limit of OM4 Multimode Fiber. Plant loss = 35 km x 0.25 dB/km + 2 connectors x 0.5 dB + splices = 10.35 dB, leaving 13.65 dB (>= 3.0 dB required margin). Receiver overload check: Tx(max) 4.0 dBm - 10.35 dB = -6.35 dBm exceeds the -7.0 dBm overload point, so a 2 dB inline attenuator is required.

rationale.subject: Dual-homed failover
rationale.justification: Every remote site has two physically diverse paths. Explicit OSPF costs make the dark-fiber path primary; the EVPL path stays in the LSDB as a hot standby. When BFD declares the primary down, SPF selects the secondary with no manual action.

rationale.subject: Metro QoS policy
rationale.decision: LLQ: EF priority 20%, AF41 40%, fair-queue rest
rationale.justification: Voice (DSCP EF) gets a strict-priority queue capped at 20% so jitter stays low without starving other classes; FinTech trading flows (DSCP AF41 or any flow to the colo trading subnet) get a 40% bandwidth guarantee; everything else uses fair-queueing. Applied outbound on every metro interface because congestion happens at egress.

rationale.subject: ACL COLO-PROTECT
rationale.justification: Applied outbound on the VLAN 40 gateway interface, i.e. it filters traffic destined to hosts in that VLAN. 7 entries, most specific first, ending in an explicit deny so denied flows are logged. Wildcard masks are computed bitwise from each subnet prefix (wildcard = ~mask & 0xFFFFFFFF).
